candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — provide and receive handoff of care (report) on assigned clients
candidate.educational_objective: Give a focused handoff that communicates current instability, recent changes, unresolved results, treatment response and follow-up needs.

options.A: A complete narrative of the hospitalization from admission onward, including the names of each clinician who participated in the client’s care.
options.B: Only the most recent vital signs and medication list, because pending diagnostic information should be reviewed independently after handoff.
options.C: The current condition, recent deterioration, oxygen requirement, pending CT result, response to the antibiotic, and actions requiring follow-up.
options.D: The original admitting diagnosis and baseline assessment, with detailed historical information deferred until the oncoming nurse reads the full chart.

candidate.rationale: A safe handoff must give the receiving nurse the information needed to continue care without a gap: the client's current condition, recent deterioration, present oxygen need, unresolved diagnostic result, response to newly started therapy, and actions requiring follow-up. A long historical narrative or a limited snapshot of vitals and medications can omit time-sensitive risks. Joint Commission's 2026 National Performance Goal framework specifically requires a handoff communication process and timely communication of important test results.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Safe handoff requires a process that communicates current condition, time-sensitive changes, unresolved results and follow-up needs so care can continue without a gap.
candidate.source_document_title: The Joint Commission — National Performance Goal #1: Right Patient, Right Care
candidate.source_locator: Joint Commission NPG #1 Right Patient, Right Care — hand-off communications, timely critical test results, recognition/response to condition changes

candidate.stem: During handoff, an unstable client has worsening oxygen needs, a CT result still pending, and the first dose of a new antibiotic just given. Which information is most important for the oncoming nurse to receive?
